question: Should OpenClaw ship the opt-in agent-authored custom-widget execution surface once the concrete review blockers are fixed and lifecycle proof is complete?
rationale: The five implementation defects have concrete repairs, but accepting a bundled unauthenticated asset route plus sandboxed agent-authored browser code is a durable product and security-boundary choice that automation cannot make.

options.title: Ship after hardening
options.body: Keep custom widgets in this PR, require all listed fixes plus end-to-end security lifecycle proof, then obtain explicit owner review.

options.title: Land built-ins first
options.body: Split out the workspace store, tools, CLI, and trusted built-in widgets while deferring custom widget execution to a narrower follow-up.

options.title: Do not bundle custom code
options.body: Keep agent-authored widget execution outside the bundled plugin and retain only trusted built-in workspace composition.

recommendation.title: Ship after hardening
recommendation.body: Keep custom widgets in this PR, require all listed fixes plus end-to-end security lifecycle proof, then obtain explicit owner review.

likelyOwner.reason: Current-main provenance and the live PR dependency-guard context connect Peter Steinberger to the plugin-tab, Plugin SDK, HTTP serving, persistence, and security decision surfaces.
